name: Mark attendance for an individual lecture rather than once for the whole day
priorityReason: A student present at registration and absent by the fourth period is invisible to daily marking.

goal.capability: to mark attendance for my own lecture
goal.outcome: the school can see who attended which period, not merely who arrived in the morning

secondaryActors.involvement: Reviews attendance across periods and makes any change after the teacher's hour has passed.

additional.description: A period ends unmarked and is flagged to the Coordinator (BR-10).

preconditions.condition: A timetable exists for the day, with the lecture scheduled to the acting teacher.
An authenticated session exists and the lecture is assigned to the acting user.
The date is a working day.
Any approved leave for the date has been applied.

postConditions: Every student scheduled for the period carries a mark for that period alone.
The period's record is stored separately from every other period, so the day can be compared across them.
Approved leave was applied before the teacher began, so a child on sanctioned leave is not marked absent in any period.
Any change carries who made it and when, and the previous mark stays visible.
A student present in the morning and missing by the fourth period is visible, which daily marking alone cannot show.
The Coordinator can read the day across periods and see where a class thinned out.
Nothing was marked for a period that was not scheduled, or on a day the school was closed.

businessRules.rule: Attendance is marked per period, and each period's record is stored separately. A day's marks are not one figure but a sequence.
A teacher marks only the lectures the timetable assigns to them. A lecture nobody was scheduled to teach cannot be marked.
A mark applies to that period alone. Marking a student absent in the fourth period says nothing about the fifth.
Approved leave is applied before the teacher begins, so a child on sanctioned leave is not marked absent in any period.
A teacher may change what they marked for one hour after saving.
Every change is logged with who made it and when, and the previous mark stays visible.
Once the teacher's hour has passed the teacher can no longer change it, and the change is made by the Coordinator.
Period attendance can be compared across the day. A student present for three periods and absent for the rest is the pattern this use case exists to reveal, and daily marking cannot show it.
Period marking and daily marking are separate records. Where a school uses both, neither overwrites the other and the two are read side by side.
A period that ends unmarked is flagged to the Coordinator, because an unmarked lecture is a class nobody accounted for.
No attendance is marked on an off-day or a holiday, or for a period the timetable did not schedule.
A student added to the section part way through the term is markable from their placement date onward.

Lists the students scheduled for that period with any approved leave already applied.

basicFlow.userAction: Marks attendance for that period only.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds the marks for this period without touching any other period's record.
Stores the record separately from every other period, records who saved and when, and starts the correction window.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the change in the same way, with the Coordinator as the person who made it.

alternateFlows.condition: A student is present for the first three periods and absent for the rest
alternateFlows.behaviour: The pattern is visible because each period is stored separately. Daily marking would have shown only that the child arrived (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher marked a student absent who was at a school activity
alternateFlows.navigation: Mark lecture attendance → Correct a mark
alternateFlows.behaviour: The mark is changed within the hour with a note, and the previous mark stays visible (BR-5, BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher's hour has passed and a change is needed
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Attendance → Attendance across periods → Correct a mark
alternateFlows.behaviour: The teacher asks and the Coordinator makes the change. The teacher cannot make it themselves (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The school also marks attendance once a day
alternateFlows.behaviour: The two records are separate and neither overwrites the other. Where both are used they are read side by side (BR-9).

alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Attendance → Attendance across periods → Unmarked
alternateFlows.behaviour: The period is flagged and chased, since an unmarked lecture is a class nobody accounted for (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A substitute teacher takes the lecture
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Attendance → Attendance across periods → Open period
alternateFlows.behaviour: The Coordinator marks it, since the lecture is not assigned to the substitute in the timetable (BR-2).

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
